pages.text: Two counter-rotating rings of bending radius 600 m cross at the detector. Heavy ions make quark-gluon plasma; protons make whatever √s allows.

$(thing)Set$(): Dipole field B, RF voltage V, Quadrupole gradient G, Beam current I.$(br2)$(thing)Disturbance$(): Dipole field error (power-supply ripple, magnet hysteresis): the beam sees B·(1 ± 0.4%·d).

$(thing)Limits$(): RF cannot replace the synchrotron loss: beam lost; Quadrupoles too weak: the beam is not focused; Quadrupoles too strong: betatron motion unstable; Space-charge tune shift too large: the beam blows up; Beam halo scraping the vacuum chamber; Interlock: dipoles and quadrupoles not superconducting (too warm).$(br2)$(thing)Rate$(): Collision rate: the beam current, times how well the lattice focuses (best at μ = 90°).

$(thing)Equations$()$(br)Effective dipole field: B_eff = B·(1 + δ_field)$(br)Beam momentum p: p = 0.2998·q·B·ρ$(br)Total energy E: E = √(p² + m²)$(br)Kinetic energy: E_k = E − m$(br)Lorentz factor γ: γ = E/m$(br)Velocity β: β = p/E$(br)Synchrotron loss / turn: U₀ = 6.03×10⁻¹⁸·q²·γ⁴·β³/ρ
